data.reason: Option 2 is rejected under K1. This is the first SLA revision, so I checked K1.d.f1. p95_wait_s stays at 188, max_wait_s at 385 and unfinished at 0.0, so customers get no faster service. Meanwhile their pickup promise is loosened from 120 s to 150 s. The +0.8 on-time gain (3/5 seeds improved) only relabels late pickups as on time, which is a worse promise with no measured benefit to customers. Option 1 is clearly the best for the KPI: on-time goes from 121.8 to 131.0 (+9.2, 5/5 seeds), late from 10.4 to 1.2, p95_wait_s from 188 to 81.4 and max_wait_s from 385 to 245. However, the company vote is part of the machine judgment, and option 1 lost it (A ○, B ×, C ×). Overriding a two-of-three majority is a serious governance step. It would also impose a heavy loss on C (utility 28.8 to 19.0) and raise road violations from 25.8 to 34.0, which we have not analysed. Departing from the LLM's recommendation of option 1 is deliberate. I prefer to keep v1 for this period and return in period 2 with a version of block_k=2 that the companies can accept, such as a remedy for C or an adjusted design, plus a breakdown of the added road violations. That keeps the measured gain within reach without setting a precedent of overriding the votes.
assumptions: The company vote is a binding part of the machine judgment for rule changes, and overriding it should be reserved for cases with no negotiable alternative.
The gain from block_k=2 will still be available, and can be re-proposed in a modified form, next period.
Keeping v1 for one more period causes no customer harm beyond the current baseline (late 10.4, p95_wait_s 188).
unknowns: Why B and C voted against block_k=2, and what remedy or modified threshold would change their votes.
Which road violations increase under block_k=2 and how severe they are.
Demand in period 2, and whether option 1's gain holds under different load.
How customers perceive the current 120 s pickup promise compared with 150 s.
